narrative:
The model determined that you have a 28% chance of representing a bad credit risk. While this is not an extremely high probability, it was enough for the bank to deny your loan application.

The three factors that most strongly influenced this decision were the status of your checking account, the loan amount you requested, and your installment rate as a percentage of disposable income. Your checking account status was the most important factor and pushed the prediction toward bad credit risk. Having a negative balance (under 0 DM) is relatively uncommon among approved applicants, where most maintain either no checking account or positive balances. This signaled higher risk to the model.

The amount you requested and your installment rate both worked in your favor, pulling the prediction toward approval. You asked for 3643 DM, which is only moderately above the average of approved loans, and your installment rate of 1% of disposable income is notably lower than the typical 3% seen in approved cases. These positive elements helped reduce the overall risk score.

Unfortunately, the negative influence from your checking account status outweighed these advantages. To improve your chances on a future application, focus first on bringing your checking account into positive territory and maintaining it there for several months. This single change would likely have the biggest impact on how a similar model would evaluate you next time.
